title: Larger x-coordinate where a line meets a parabola
source: Theory IGCSE-18.4 Quick check 1 (y=x^2-4x+5 and y=x+1; larger x is 4); book Worked example 11-12 style, pp.605-606
stem: The graphs of \(y=x^2+({B|int})x+({C|int})\) and \(y=x+({k|int})\) meet at two points. Write down the larger of the two \(x\)-coordinates of those points.

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: Substitute \(y=x+({k|int})\) into the curve and rearrange: the roots are \(x=({r|int})\) and \(x=({s|int})\)

steps.name: A
steps.note: r is larger than s by the constraint r>s.

contexts.note: Includes the original r=4, s=1, k=1, which is y=x^2-4x+5 and y=x+1

contexts.stem: Solve \(x+({k|int})=x^2+({B|int})x+({C|int})\) and write down the larger root.

stem: The graphs of \(y=\dfrac{({Q|int})}{x}\) and \(y=x\) meet at two points. Write down the positive \(x\)-coordinate of a meeting point.

steps.name: A
steps.note: n is positive in the parameter range.

title: Product of the x-coordinates of the meeting points
source: Theory IGCSE-18.4 Quick check 3 (product of x-coordinates 1 and 4 is 4); same graphs as Quick check 1
stem: The graphs of \(y=x^2+({B|int})x+({C|int})\) and \(y=x+({k|int})\) meet at two points. Find the product of the two \(x\)-coordinates of those points.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The \(x\)-coordinates are \(({r|int})\) and \(({s|int})\), and their product is \({A|int}\)
steps.note: For the monic quadratic obtained after substitution, the product of the roots is the constant term.

contexts.note: Includes the original r=4, s=1, k=1

title: Solve y=x^2-3x-13 and y=x-1

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2021). Official answers and mark allocation from the MS PDF. Fully manual; no auto-credit.

stem:
This question is 0580/23/O/N/21 Question 22, taken from the official QP.

Solve the simultaneous equations.
You must show all your working.

\(y=x^2-3x-13\)

\(y=x-1\)

steps.name: EQ
steps.text_tex: Equate (or substitute): \(x^2-3x-13=x-1\), which rearranges to \(x^2-4x-12=0\). (The equivalent quadratic in \(y\) is \(y^2-2y-15=0\).)

steps.name: FAC
steps.note: MS: (x-6)(x+2) [=0] M1, or correct factors for their quadratic, or correct use of the quadratic formula or completing the square for their equation.

steps.name: P1
steps.note: MS: B2 for both pairs; B1 for one correct pair, or two correct x values, or two correct y values.

steps.name: P2
steps.note: Official answers: (6, 5) and (-2, -3). If B0 is scored and at least 2 method marks are scored, SC1 is available for correct substitution of both of their x values or their y values.
